native_model: Self-organizing recurrent neural network (SORN) account of motor-sequence learning with STDP, intrinsic plasticity, synaptic normalization and supervised output readout
memory_representation_state: learned recurrent synaptic structure and thresholds retain sequence-dependent structure; raw stimulus/training sequence is external input history
prediction_state: next/internal sequence dynamics are generated by recurrent network but are not a separate persistent prediction-coordinator variable
action_skill_variables: supervised motor-output classification/readout driven by recurrent state
observations: target output labels during supervised readout training
retrieval_readout_rules: trained supervised motor-output readout from recurrent network state
prediction_generation_operators: recurrent dynamics generate sequence-sensitive internal state evolution; no separate forward model is source-defined
learning_plasticity_rules: STDP + intrinsic plasticity + synaptic normalization; supervised output training remains distinct
negative_adverse_results: The SORN is a computational neural-network account fitted qualitatively to human sequence-learning effects; it is not a direct measurement of STDP/IP/synaptic normalization in participants.
The task-specific motor output/readout is supervised and externally defined; the recurrent network should not be mislabeled as an endogenous inverse motor model.
Interference and facilitation emerge from inherited SORN plasticity architecture; they are not evidence that this paper independently invented the SORN family.
anti_conflation_assertions: training schedule is external and not itself the learning operator
external target/output label is not internal skill state
learned weights are source-defined retained network state, not an added coordinator
supervised readout is distinct from recurrent representation
offline/training-induced plasticity is not evidence for a separate online coordination module
